mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a single month leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the rate hike, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a two-year backtest.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10,000 jobs for three consecutive months coincides with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant return over the 60-day horizon, or the effect persists only during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 6.0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% followed within one month by a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,200K units predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it signals a shift from contraction to expansion in business activity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >2% in a month AND HOUST rises >1,200K in the following month
regime_hint: Transition from contraction to expansion phase
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or insignificant, or the pattern recurs during periods of high financial volatility (RSAFS > 5,000K).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-month decline in the goods price index (INDPRO) below 100, when combined with a decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5%, predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects excess supply and weak demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4.5% in the same window
regime_hint: Structural supply shock with labor market loosening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 12-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 208 for three consecutive months, without a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE), signals disinflation and supports a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls <208 for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE remains flat or declining
regime_hint: Disinflationary trend in a steady labor market
failure_condition: No significant forward return over 60 days, or CPI declines are reversed before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-month drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% triggers a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it reflects strong labor demand and corporate hiring optimism.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant forward return observed in the next 5 days, or the effect persists only during high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 210).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in retail sales (PAYEMS) of at least 20,000 jobs followed within 10 days by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals shifting consumer and supply priorities.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases ≥20,000 in a month AND INDPRO falls >1% in the following week
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the pattern is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent 6-month decline in the 10-year Treasury yield (implied by FEDFUNDS) below 3.5% predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as lower discount rates boost equity present-value valuations.
regime_hint: Low-rate environment sustained for multiple quarters
failure_condition: No significant forward return observed over 60 days, or the yield decline reverses before the horizon.
